shortDescription: Costco NASDAQ:COST delivered another better-than-expected quarter with a top- and bottom-line beat, above-consensus growth in membership fees, and comparable sales that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations.The big-box retailer also reported a double-digit increase in comparable sales for its digital…

children: delivered another better-than-expected quarter with a top- and bottom-line beat, above-consensus growth in membership fees, and comparable sales that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations.
The big-box retailer also reported a double-digit increase in comparable sales for its digital channel for the 16-week period ending August 30.

Total revenue, including a 7% increase in membership fees of $1.85B (vs. $1.83B estimates), increased 12% to $95.72B, beating estimates by $830M, and contributed to a profit of $6.57 per share. The bottom line improved 15% year-over-year and was 5 cents better than expected. These results included a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per share from IEEPA tariff refunds received during the fiscal fourth quarter.

Comparable sales in the U.S. were up 7.2% on an adjusted basis (vs. 6.85% estimates), up 4.6% in Canada, and rose 6.2% in other international markets, resulting in a 9.4% increase in company-wide comparable store sales. Excluding fuel sales, total company comparable sales rose 6.7%, beating 6.44% estimates.

Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, eight more warehouses than in the fiscal third quarter, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.

title: Costco beats sales and profit expectations as comparable sales continue to surge
